cards.explanation: The answer is Bezalel son of Uri. The LORD says, "See, I have called by name Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah." Called by name, friends! I've been called plenty of things in my life, mostly "hey, you," and it never once felt like that. Out of every Israelite, God picked this one man and said his name out loud.

The answer is False, and God keeps it all on the building side. He says He has filled Bezalel with the Spirit of God, "…with skill, ability, and knowledge in all kinds of craftsmanship…" Then comes the job list: artistic works in gold, silver and bronze, cutting gemstones for settings, and carving wood. Gold, gems and wood, friends, and no battle plans anywhere. I'd call that a man you'd trust with a cookie box AND a lampstand.

The answer is True, and it keeps going! God says Bezalel will "…cut gemstones for settings, and to carve wood, so that he may be a master of every craft." Gold, silver, bronze, gems AND wood, friends. Meanwhile I get nervous when a recipe has two steps.

The answer is Oholiab son of Ahisamach. God says, "…I have selected Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, as his assistant." Notice Bezalel is from Judah and Oholiab is from Dan, so two different tribes. God also gave skill to all the craftsmen, so this is a whole team effort.
The answer is Sabbaths. The LORD says, "Surely you must keep My Sabbaths…" After all that talk about building, He turns to rest. Notice He calls them HIS Sabbaths, friends.

The answer is that He is the LORD who makes them holy. God says the Sabbath is a sign between Him and the Israelites, "…so that you may know that I am the LORD who sanctifies you." Sanctifies means He makes them holy. The Sabbath is a reminder of who is doing that work, friends, and it's Him.

The answer is True, friends, and this is a heavy one. God says, "Anyone who profanes it must surely be put to death." He also says, "Keep the Sabbath, for it is holy to you." The text shows how seriously He treats the day He calls holy.

The answers are six and seventh. God says, "For six days work may be done…" and He calls the seventh day "…a Sabbath of complete rest, holy to the LORD." Complete rest, friends! I've stamped a lot of cookies in my time, and I never turn down a day off. Even my mustache gets to sit down on that one.

The answer is that the LORD made the heavens and the earth in six days and rested on the seventh. That is the reason God gives when He says, "for in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, but on the seventh day He rested and was refreshed." The sign points back to creation, friends. It's a sign between Him and the Israelites "forever."

The answer is stone, friends! The text says they were "…tablets of stone inscribed by the finger of God." Written by the finger of God Himself. The story isn't over, either, because there's more to come after this.
